title: Conveyor: deterministic OSS-weights normalization, conversion, validation, and profile publish pipeline
creator: Ava Thompson
description: Build a single, auditable pipeline ("Conveyor") that ingests open-source model weights from community sources, normalizes storage formats, runs deterministic conversion and quantization passes, validates functional and performance characteristics, and publishes a pinned model artifact + inferred performance profile to the model catalog. The Conveyor should be resilient to flaky upstream sources, produce reproducible artifacts, and surface human-review gates for safety and license checks.
acceptance_criteria: Conveyor can fetch weights from at least 3 community registries (Hugging Face, Git LFS mirrors, OCI blobs) with retry/backoff and provenance metadata
Weights normalization step emits canonical manifest (format, hash, provenance, license) and stores raw blob in immutable storage
Deterministic conversion produces runtime-ready binaries with identical outputs across two independent runs (bitwise or within a stable float tolerance for fp32->int8 flows)
Automatic profile job runs micro-benchmarks (latency P50/P95 for common seq lengths, memory residency, KV-cache behavior) and creates a profile JSON stored in catalog
Pin recommendation engine suggests a canonical pin (model version + conversion config) and writes to catalog with human-review pending flag
Pipeline exposes clear rollback paths and idempotent rerun semantics for any stage
End-to-end telemetry (ingest time, conversion duration, benchmark results, artifactsize) visible in Console runtime-1.21 dashboard
Integration tests covering conversion -> profile publish against a small curated set of public models are green in CI
runbook_steps: Stage 0: Register upstream source URL and fetch manifest (validate signature if present)
Stage 1: Normalize weight blobs into canonical storage layout and generate canonical_manifest.json
Stage 2: Run dependency and license scanner; if flagged, create a security review ticket and pause Conveyor
Stage 3: Deterministic conversion and optional quantization path with an explicit seed and environment snapshot
Stage 4: Sanity checks: model shape, tokenizer compatibility smoke, deterministic output sample comparison
Stage 5: Performance profiling job on representative hardware dim (small GPU and large GPU), collect latency and memory metrics
Stage 6: Score and classify the artifact (latency buckets, suitability tags) and produce a profile artifact
Stage 7: Create candidate pin and publish to catalog as 'pending-review' with provenance metadata
Stage 8: Notify PM/ML-OPS for manual verification; on approval, mark pin as 'published' and trigger console indexing
notes: We intentionally separate normalization from conversion to allow re-run of conversion with new quantizers without re-fetching upstream blobs
Deterministic conversion means freezing env (containers) and toolchain versions; we will store a reproducibility digest alongside the artifact
Consider a fallback lightweight conversion (fp16) when quantizers fail to meet quality thresholds to maintain availability
Edge case: community weights sometimes omit tokenizer files. Add a tokenizer-inference heuristic that looks up model card metadata and common tokenizers
Security gating: license scanning must be pluggable; initially integrate OSS-License-Scout and an internal allowlist of permissive licenses
